quote: The exclusivity obligation in the executed agreement is materially broader than what was discussed in the Term Sheet in at least four dimensions ... If Harrowgate bottles soft drinks, water, or any non-beer product—or operates filling facilities in Europe, Latin America, or Asia—it is contractually prohibited from sourcing containers from any other supplier.
reason: The memo identifies Supply Agreement §3.1 as requiring exclusive purchase of 'all glass and PET containers' for 'any beverage product' worldwide. It contrasts this with Term Sheet §2.1, which covered amber glass, beer brands and U.S./Canadian facilities only. It treats Harrowgate as bound by the executed text, saying the client is 'contractually prohibited', and lists the Term Sheet as non-binding. It recommends narrowing §3.1 back to the agreed scope. It does not cite the §15.2 precedence or entire-agreement clause, but it captures the substance: Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed scope.
